newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends down at intraday low vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends down at intraday low vs dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at an intraday low of 8.2936 from Wednesday's 8.2925 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai due to intervention by the central bank, the People's Bank of China, late in trading, traders said.
The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2924.
Dealers said the central bank was seen intervening to depress the yuan at the last 15 minutes of trading.

The yuan opened higher at an intraday high of 8.2916 and consolidated to move around 8.2925 for most of the session before it slipped further to end at the low. Trading was active early but dull with most business done at 8.2925.
One dealer said the central bank intervened on the market after yuan's upward trend of the past few weeks.
"The intervention hurt pro-yuan sentiment on the market on Thursday, but its impact will not last because it was just done in the last few minutes of trading today," he said.
A second dealer said selling was concentrated at the 8.2920 level.
"The 8.2920 level is now regarded as the short-term resistance point and one that buyers have failed to push the yuan through in recent weeks," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to rebound on Friday to move in a range of 8.2920 and 8.2930.
The yuan closed down at 7.1800 from 7.1150 against 100 Japanese yen and lower at 1.0712 from 1.0705 against the Hong Kong dollar.
